newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CORDOVA, RINCON THROW 10-INNING NO-HITTER FOR PIRATES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CORDOVA, RINCON THROW 10-INNING NO-HITTER FOR PIRATES.

text.p: Francisco Cordova and Ricardo Rincon pitched the first combined extra-inning no-hitter in baseball history Saturday as the Pittsburgh Pirates blanked the Houston Astros 3-0.
Neither team scored until pinch-hitter Mark Smith blasted a three-run homer with two out in the bottom of the 10th.
It was the Pirates' first no-hitter since John Candelaria tossed one against Los Angeles on August 9, 1976.

Cordova, a 25-year-old right-hander, pitched the first nine innings, limiting the Astros to two walks while striking out 10. He retired 18 straight batters before Luis Gonzalez drew a two-out walk in the seventh.
"I wanted to just pitch my game," Cordova said. "I thought I could have continued to pitch. I felt tired, but thought I could still pitch some baseball."

"The decision to take Cordova out wasn't really that hard," Pirates manager Gene Lamont said. "I wouldn't have pinch-hit for him in the eighth, he deserved a chance to get a no-hitter. I wish we would have scored in the ninth, it makes it tougher in a scoreless game. Every pitch can be the game."
Rincon (3-4), a 27-year-old left-hander, walked one and struck out one in the 10th.

"I felt a lot of pressure going into the 10th inning," he conceded. "I just looked not to mess up, I didn't want to give up the first base hit for the team after a couple of bad games. Tonight, we played our kind of game."
But the game remained scoreless into the ninth as Chris Holt and Billy Wagner shut Pittsburgh down into extra innings.

John Hudek (0-1) started the 10th and struck out Dale Sveum before walking Jason Kendall. Jose Guillen lined to centre, but pinch-hitter Turner Ward walked and Smith, batting for Rincon, crushed an 0-1 pitch deep over the left-field fence for just his third homer of the season.
It ended the Pirates' 28-inning scoreless drought. Pittsburgh had been shut out in the first two games of the series and had not scored since the eighth inning of Sunday's 6-3 victory at St. Louis.
"(After) the fact that we hadn't scored in 27 innings, you couldn't beat this," Lamont said.

Cordova had given up 10 runs and 16 hits over 14 innings in his two previous starts, but pitched a two-hitter at Houston on June 23 for his second shutout of the season. This was just the second time in his last seven outings in which Rincon was not scored upon.
Houston had three solid chances at a hit.
Cordova made a barehanded pickup of Derek Bell's slow roller and threw him out to end the seventh.
Shortstop Kevin Collier ranged behind second base to field Brad Ausmus' grounder in the eighth.
First baseman Kevin Young made an over-the-shoulder catch on Tim Bogar's pop-up in shallow right field to end the eighth.

"He just kept us off balance," Gonzalez said of Cordova. "The first thing you know, you're in the top of the 10th with no hits and a 0-0 game. It's still a game, you still have to win it. I don't think we were really concerned about the no-hitter at that point."
A sellout crowd of 44,119 at Three Rivers Stadium saw the first combined no-hitter in Pirates history.

The Astros were no-hit victims for the third time in franchise history. San Francisco's Juan Marichal did it to them in a 1-0 victory on June 15, 1963, as did Cincinnati's Jim Maloney in a 10-0 rout on April 30, 1969.
